text:
maria: Heads up — hit a weird flake on L4 during a sustained canary. One request saw the kernel swap from the L4-optimized attention path to the fallback path mid-stream and the response had truncated KV segments. Not confident this is purely a probe timeout.

tyler: ugh, seen that too on stress runs. probably a race between capability probe finishing and the kernel chooser re-evaluating. happens when qps spikes and we evict probe result? :thinking_face:

sasha: can you paste the logs? curious whether it was `probe_result=OK` then `probe_evicted` or a latency hop.

maria: paste below (sanitized):
```
[2169001234.112] req=0x7f8a probe_start device=L4
[2169001234.118] req=0x7f8a probe_ok kernels=[l4_attn_fast]
[2169001234.119] chooser=select l4_attn_fast
[2169001234.125] probe_evicted key=l4_cap_v1 ttl=0
[2169001234.128] chooser=reselect fallback_kernel=generic_attn
[2169001234.135] req=0x7f8a resume with generic_attn
```

ken: interesting. eviction at .125 suggests our cache TTL or LRU policy gets overly aggressive under memory pressure. but even if evicted, chooser should honor the active decision for in-flight requests.

eva: agreed. two independent problems: (1) the capability cache eviction semantics vs in-flight decision lifetime; (2) the chooser logic re-evaluating mid-request instead of pinning kernel instance. both need contract-level fixes.

tyler: proposals:
- keep a per-request kernel lease pinned from selection until completion (cheap pointer + refcount)
- make probe cache entries immutable for the duration of any active lease counters
- add probe metadata `capability_version` and `probe_epoch` to avoid TTBR races

sasha: +1. also we should ensure attention-optimizer-specific state (KV cache layout, quantization path flags) is consistent with the pinned kernel. otherwise we get memory layout mismatch like we saw.

maria: example failure mode: pinned kernel expects KV layout A (packed u8), fallback expects layout B (packed fp16). mid-request swap leaves KV in A but fallback reads B -> truncated tokens.

runtime-bot: [PROBE] device=L4 id=0 probe_ok=true kernels=[l4_attn_fast] ver=3 epoch=21690012

ken: runtime-bot logs confirm ver=3 epoch=21690012. but eviction shows no epoch guard. maybe probe cache eviction callback doesn't decrement active lease counter.

eva: long-term refactor idea: split detection (probe) from policy (chooser). detection writes to a capability registry (append-only with monotonic epoch). chooser reads registry snapshots and makes immutable choices per-request. registry GC can compact epochs but never mutate earlier epochs in-place.

tyler: that sounds robust. short-term we can implement per-request lease and bump probe cache TTL for L4/H100 A100 hot paths.

sasha: any perf impact to pinning kernels via refcounting? we allocate a tiny refcount object per request, should be negligible compared to kernel exec. important to avoid global locks.

ken: implement as atomic ref on kernel_entry struct + hazard pointer-style pointer maintenance. no global locks.

maria: also want to note attention optimizations differ by arch: H100 has TF32-wide attention kernels that assume fp32 scratch; A100 kernels use fp16 with different block sizes; L4 uses int8 quantized kernels. The chooser must surface these differences as explicit capability flags (`attn_layout={fp32_scratch,fp16_block16,int8_packed}`) so that KV/IO layers can select layout converters when necessary.

eva: yes. contract proposal for detection output:
```
{ "device": "L4", "capabilities": ["int8_packed_attn","kv_prefix_sharing"], "epoch": 21690012, "version": "3" }
```
Make it a typed protobuf for forward compatibility.

tyler: small RFC follow-up: add fields `lease_duration_ms` and `pinned_until` to selection trace so that SLO debugging can show why a kernel was kept.

sasha: can we add a canary rollout plan? we should verify under high qps with induced probe evictions and force mid-request chooser re-eval to confirm fixes.

maria: plan:
- short-term (hotfix) -> pin per-request kernel lease + bump L4 probe TTL to 10s. (owner: tyler)
- mid-term -> add epoch/version handshake to probe result + prevent mutating registry epochs in-place (owner: sasha)
- long-term -> capability registry refactor + typed protobuf + chooser snapshotting + GC compaction (owner: eva)
- verification -> chaos test that forces eviction mid-request and validates no kernel swap (owner: ken)

ken: I'll add the chaos test to eng-runtime repo and wire it to the perf-canary harness.

ev a: can someone file an RFC follow-up and attach the logs above? I'll consolidate and drive the registry refactor.

maria: created thread in rfc board: https://rfc.internal/PROPOSAL-487 (notes copied)

tyler: I'll open a small PR for the lease hotfix this afternoon.

sasha: ack. will prioritize the epoch handshake patch next week.

runtime-bot: [DEPLOY] rolling canary: kernel-lease-hotfix -> 3 nodes (L4 pool)

maria: thanks all. tagging @eng-oncall if we see regressions during the canary.

tyler: ping me if you see any odd remaining truncation.

maria: closing the thread when canary stable. :white_check_mark:
